question: A bare cairn librarian launches a browser whose request arrives at the web server's shim (9.6.1), so that shim must already hold the port. Who starts the web server's shim: (a) the librarian's shim, waking it over the bus before it launches the browser; (b) the ground loop, which every shim already starts, starting the one web server shim on its box (18.3.5); or (c) the host, by systemd socket activation on port 80, so the first request itself starts the shim?
why_it_blocks: Outline 9.6.1 has the browser's http request ARRIVE at the web server's shim, so that shim must be listening before the librarian's shim launches the browser; the web server shim's design (who binds the port, and when) cannot be built until this is settled.
answer: (b), by the outline: the ground loop's pulse starts the web server's shim like every other declared instance, and the librarian's chain only needs the shim to already be there. CairnComponentOutline.txt: "5.8.3.4.1 The ground loop finds one pulse.py per device. pulse.py reads its own device's declared instances (5.7.3.4) and pulses each one, so the ground loop never needs to know instances exist. Pulsing an instance that isn't connected is what starts its shim." | "8.6.1 ... That http request arrives at the web server's shim, which launches the web server ... Each part is self-initializing (5.3.5)." | "15.3.5 It runs on one box, so a box that joins the instance starts no web server of its own".
